title: Corned Beef Hash Breakfast
subtitle: Crisp diced potatoes and corned beef with eggs cracked on top.
description: Corned beef and potatoes crisped in a skillet with eggs on top. Diner classic scaled for the firehall — especially good after St. Patrick's or leftover corned beef.

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.notes: plus salt to taste—corned beef is salty

ingredients.name: fresh parsley
ingredients.notes: chopped, plus hot sauce at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Corned Beef Hash Breakfast in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Par-cook potatoes
steps.instruction: Microwave diced potatoes with a splash of water in a covered bowl until just tender, about 8 minutes. Drain thoroughly and spread on a towel to dry—wet potatoes will steam instead of crisp.

steps.title: Crisp the hash base
steps.instruction: Heat oil in two large skillets over medium-high until shimmering. Add potatoes in a single layer without crowding; let sit 4 minutes for crust before stirring. Cook until deeply golden on most sides.

steps.title: Add corned beef and onion
steps.instruction: Fold in onion, pepper, and corned beef. Press the mixture into the pan and cook undisturbed 3 minutes to build a crust. Season with pepper; taste before adding salt because corned beef carries plenty.

steps.title: Make wells for eggs
steps.instruction: Divide hash between warm serving skillets or one large cast iron. Make eight shallow wells and crack an egg into each. Season eggs with pepper.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Corned Beef Hash Breakfast onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Cover and finish eggs
steps.instruction: Cover skillets over medium-low heat until egg whites are fully set (165°F) and yolks are runny or jammy to preference. Scatter parsley and serve straight from the pan with hot sauce.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Corned Beef Hash Breakfast — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

stationWorkflow: Dry potatoes aggressively—this is the difference between diner hash and cafeteria mush.
Use two skillets in parallel if one pan cannot fit eight eggs without crowding.
Serve family-style from cast iron so the crew gets the crisp bottom layer first.
cleanupNotes: Deglaze hash pans with hot water while warm; corned beef fat sets hard if left to cool.
Scrape potato starch from cutting boards immediately before it dries and glues itself on.
leftovers: Reheat hash covered at 325°F for 12 minutes; fry fresh eggs to order on top rather than reheating set yolks.
Press cold leftovers into patties and griddle until crisp for handheld hash cakes at the next breakfast.
